title: Cleo and the slap bass
summary: Breaux describes Cleo's triplet slap bass, how it works, how long he was popular, and his death on a merchant ship in the war.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well who was the star during that when you were a kid?

What bass soloist? Well this fellow I told you about before, he got killed at sea. Cleo? Cleo had a wonderful slap. Well at that time it was a novelty to play slap bass. Very much novelty because he used to play it with a triplet effect. I've seen you do that. Yeah I couldn't do it but I mean I've gotten out of practice because slap bass is just about out of style. Now you better tell them here anybody playing slap bass. Not even when you're picking. If your bass is strong so that the string is going to slap back on you. Some fellows got such a heavy pull, they have to raise their strings higher than others. That's to avoid the slap back that the string will give. But the back you don't ever hear any bass player playing slap bass anymore.
In the slap bass do you actually take your hand and hit the string against the fingerboard or even it snaps back?

You do it both ways. You slap your hand on the bass bass and you pull the string out very hard and let it slap back and then you come right back with a slap that makes the three licks and it'll be done real fair. And give you a triplet effect. And Cleo was exceptionally great on that. It was nice doing that time because it was just something new. People liked it just like the same as any other novelty. It comes out and it's good when it first started. And after a while it dies out just like anything else.
What did he take? Two bars? Or 12 bars? Or 16 bars?

Or 32? Or what? Cleo. Oh, he'd take the whole course. He'd play all night long if they'd just let him. His band just had to come on in and take him out because he gets good to him and he just works with it.
By what year was that? How old was that?

Cleo was popular from I'd say as far as I can remember from around 29 or 30 up until the war started. He got killed on a merchant ship because he went to the merchant marine and the ship he was on was bombed somewhere out of sea. But he was very popular around New Orleans as a bass player. Very nice bass player. I used to like his playing and I used to like his solo work because I just like that slap effect he had. I mean I can slap a little but I never could perfect it as well as Cleo. He is real good. I think Chester can do a little of that kind of work too. Chester's always. Chester's good at straight picking and he's wonderful on the bull. And he's got a way of picking with the end of his bull. He turns his bull backwards and you pick with it like a stick in. A little frog down the screen. That's right.
